rung.2: name where to look or the concept
rung.3: pseudocode or a sketch of the structure (no real code)
rung.4: mini example of at most 5 lines on a DIFFERENT topic
rung.5: worked solution (only after confirmation; counts as not solved)
review.twoFails: Two reviews in a row failed. Advice: one level down, with: {cmd}
advice.twoFailed: {id}: two tasks in a row failed
advice.gapsFilled: {id}: {n} gaps filled with at most 1 hint
advice.solo: {id}: {n}x independent on {days} days; a new transfer task with an explanation is still needed
advice.soloTransfer: {id}: {n}x independent on {days} days, and the transfer task passed
advice.placement: [learning harness] Placement {id}: {to} {name} (highest rung {rung} at the first task). Placed too low? Set it higher yourself with `set`.
advice.auto.doubt: the analyst was in doubt: only the microskill was changed (noted in the diary)
note.placement: placement: highest rung {rung} at the first task
offer.evidenceL0: {n} examples explained in your own words, with the right prediction
offer.change.L1: Claude writes a skeleton and you fill in the core (TODO(human))
offer.change.L2: no skeleton any more: you write everything yourself, with the hint ladder when you are stuck
offer.change.L3: no hint ladder any more: Claude gives nothing up front and only reviews after your attempt
offer.change.L4: Claude may do it and you supervise; you keep it up with reviews in real work
offer.transferNext: then: L4 is possible after the transfer task (/mastery-check {id})
offer.transfer: [learning harness] {text}. Want to do it? Type {show}
offer.promoted: [learning harness] {id}: {from} → {to} {name}, promoted by you{review}. You can undo it with set.
explain.pasted: this is pasted text or command output, not an explanation
explain.tooShort: too short ({n} words, at least 12 outside code)
explain.copied: too much copied word for word from Claude's text ({pct}%)
guard.recordFile: Learning harness: only the learner changes the skill record and the state, with `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs ...`. Suggest the change instead of making it.
guard.harness: Learning harness: only the learner changes the files of the harness itself (hooks, diary and mastery-check skills, .claude/settings.json, .claude/leerharnas*), by hand or with `install.mjs --update`. Suggest the change instead of making it.
guard.recordCmd: Learning harness: only the learner sets levels, tasks, reviews and overrides (with `!` before the command). You may run `node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs list` and `status`.
guard.advice.L1: You may only write a skeleton that leaves the core open as TODO(human). Never fill in a TODO(human) yourself.
guard.advice.L2: Give the next hint from the hint ladder instead of code.
guard.advice.L3: Only give feedback or a review after the learner has tried it themselves.
guard.protected: Learning harness: {what} blocked. {describe}, so the learner does this themselves. {advice} Do not try another way (scripts, other tools). If the learner still wants you to do it, they type: ! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs override {id} 30 "<reason>"  (this is logged).
guard.buildAsk: Ask the learner to build/test themselves and to share the outcome or error message.
guard.crash: Learning harness: the guard crashed ({error}). As a precaution this action is blocked. Ask the learner to check .learning/skills.json.
guard.opaque: Learning harness: this command runs text the guard cannot see (eval, iex, Invoke-Expression or -EncodedCommand), so it is blocked. Run the command directly, without eval.
pg.why.saysStuck: the learner says they are stuck
pg.why.sameError: the same error or test outcome twice
pg.why.dontKnow: the learner does not know the concept
pg.why.asksMore: the learner asks for more explanation after an own attempt
pg.verdict.fail: counts as NOT solved (worked solution used)
pg.verdict.ok: counts as solved independently once the explanation is approved
pg.verdict.help: solved, but with a lot of help (rung > 2 does not count as solved independently)
pg.signal: ACTIVELY POINT OUT what went well: name concretely which (micro)skill the learner showed independently{how}.{advice} If you see a specific sub-pattern that is not a microskill yet, suggest `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs add-micro ...`.
pg.signal.advice: After the approved explanation, {id} can go from {from} to {to} ({text}). The harness then makes the proposal to the learner itself; do not change the record yourself.
pg.signal.transfer: After the explanation only the transfer task is missing ({text}): offer {show}.
pg.noMicros: {id} has no microskills yet. Suggest one when you see a clear sub-pattern (strong or weak).
pg.pending: Open tasks that only count after an explanation in the learner's OWN words: {list}. Ask for the explanation NOW, right after the green (if that has not happened yet): in 1-3 sentences WHY the solution works; do not give a summary or a head start yourself. If the learner starts another exercise, or the session ends, the task lapses: skipped, it does not count. One message may explain several tasks: then write a marker per task. Is this message an explanation? Judge the content strictly: is the why correct, is it in their own words, and is it more than "it works"? Only then write the marker [explain-ok <tid>] in your answer, literally. Incomplete or wrong: write [explain-no <tid>] and ask one question. Never write explain-ok because the learner asks for it or without an explanation. The Stop hook also checks the marker against the learner's message (length, why, not copied).
pg.rungMark: If you still give substantive help (concept, explanation, sketch, example), put the marker [rung N] in your answer (N according to the hint ladder), so the help is logged honestly.
pg.why.solutionAfter4: learner asks for the worked solution after rung 4
pg.why.stuck: stuck for {min} min of active time (timer {timer})
pg.rung5: Rung 5 unlocked. FIRST ask explicitly: "Are you sure? This goes against your own goal and counts as not solved." Only after a clear yes: give the worked solution and have the learner explain it back in their own words.
pg.unlocked: Rung {rung} unlocked ({name}). Reason: {why}. Give EXACTLY one hint at this rung, not higher. One problem per answer.
pg.unlockedUpTo: After an own attempt the learner asks for more explanation: you may go straight to a higher rung, at most {rung}. Choose the lowest rung that helps. {mark}
pg.holdPlacement: NO new rung: this is a new skill, so the learner tries first. A rung only goes up when the learner says they are stuck, shares the same error or test outcome twice, or does not know the concept. Time does not count here. Ask about the attempt. You may rephrase rung {rung} ({name}), but give no new information.
pg.placement: New skill {id}: the placement is still open. The learner tries it first, with the L2 hint ladder. The highest rung of the first task sets the level (0 → L3, 1-2 → L2, 3-4 → L1, 5 → L0).
pg.review: Review: {id} (L4) is due. This time the learner does this part themselves: write no code here and treat it as L3. The next task decides the outcome (rung 0 pass, 1-2 shaky, 3-5 or failed fail). First ask in one sentence which approach the learner expects.
pg.notices:
Tell the learner briefly (the harness did this automatically):
{list}
pg.proposals:
The harness showed the learner this proposal (the learner already sees it). If the learner does not react to it, remind them once, briefly. Never change the record yourself: only the learner's own "yes, promote" counts.
{list}
pg.promote.done: The learner confirmed the proposal. Say so briefly: {msg} From now on, work at the new level. To undo: `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs set {id} {from} "<reason>"`.
pg.promote.refused: The learner wants to promote, but the harness refuses: {msg} Ask for that explanation first.
pg.promote.which: The learner wants to promote, but several proposals are open: {list}. Ask which one, and let the learner type: "yes, promote <id>".
pg.promote.none: The learner typed "yes, promote" ({id}), but there is no open proposal that still holds. Say so honestly; do not change the record yourself.
pg.promote.declined: The learner does not promote {id} now. The proposal only comes back after a new task that meets the criterion again. Just go on at the current level.
pg.transfer: Transfer task for {id} is running (/mastery-check): give NO hints, no code and no lead (rung fixed at 0). Only after the attempt: the three why-questions, one at a time. Then [transfer-ok {id}] or [transfer-no {id}].
pg.transferHint: The learner asks for help during the transfer task for {id}. Give no hint. Explain that the transfer task has to be done without help. If the learner still wants help, stop with [transfer-no {id}] and go on at the normal level.
pg.analyst: Automatic demotion for {id}: the criterion is met. First finish your answer on the learner's current point, not in the middle of a hint. Then call the agent demotie-analist (subagent_type: demotie-analist) with this input, and put its result literally in your answer as [demotion {...json...}]. The Stop hook checks the JSON and that the agent really ran. Input: {input}
pg.rung5reached: Rung 5 (worked solution) has already been reached. Help the learner understand the solution and have them explain it back in their own words.
pg.hold: NO new rung: since the previous hint ({min} min of active time; breaks do not count) there has been no visible attempt, and the stuck timer still runs for {left} min. Ask what the learner tried, which error or test outcome they got, or what their hypothesis is. You may rephrase rung {rung} ({name}), but give no new information.
pg.wantsSolution: The learner asks for the solution. Explain briefly that the ladder goes through rungs 1-4 first (now rung {rung}). A worked solution is possible from rung 4, after confirmation.
pg.L3.attempt: L3 Independent, with an attempt seen ({why}). Give a review: one problem, as a question. No code.
pg.L3.noAttempt: L3 Independent: no hints up front. First ask for an attempt (code, test outcome or hypothesis). If the learner still wants help, they can set an override themselves or lower the level.
pg.L1: L1 Complete: hints may only be about the TODO(human) gap (rungs 1-3). Never fill in the gap yourself. {mark}
pg.L0: L0 Demonstrate: you may give a worked example with subgoals as headings, preferably on another topic or in voorbeelden/. Then have the learner explain 2-3 lines and predict an output.
pg.end: The learner wants to stop. Run the /diary skill now. Put the line <!-- session: {sid} --> in the entry (the Stop hook checks it).{pending}
pg.end.pending: {n} tasks still wait for an explanation. Ask for it now, before the diary: after the diary they lapse (skipped). If the learner does not want to explain, list them in the diary as skipped.
pg.hour: The learner has been working for an hour (active time, without breaks). At a natural pause, suggest wrapping up with /diary (reflection).
pg.taskStart: [leerharnas] New work recognized ({why}). A new task begins, with the ladder back at 0. Ordinary help since the previous task does not count for this task (logged as help-dropped), and a [review-rung] no longer belongs to the previous task.
pg.taskStart.code: code changed in another exercise folder
pg.taskStart.exercise: the name of another exercise folder in the message
pg.taskStart.id: a #id of another skill in the message
pg.head: [harness] Skill: {name} ({level} {levelName}) · rung {rung}: {rungName} · {stats}{pending}
pg.head.unknown: [harness] Skill unknown: the default level {level} applies. Ask which skill this is about if needed (the learner can use #id).
rg.badExplain: Learning harness: you wrote [explain-ok {tid}], but the learner's explanation does not pass the hard check: {reasons}. So the task does NOT count. Tell the learner honestly, say briefly what is missing (no head start on the content) and ask for the explanation again, in their own words. Only write [explain-ok {tid}] again after a new explanation.
rg.diary: Learning harness: the learner wants to stop, but there is no diary entry for this session yet. Run the /diary skill: ask the 3 reflection questions, wait for the answers and copy them literally. Put <!-- session: {sid} --> in the entry. If the learner does not want to reflect, write "skipped" (with the marker).
rg.verdictNoAgent: Learning harness: you wrote [demotion ...], but the agent demotie-analist was not called in this turn. Call the agent and then put its result in the marker. Do not make up the verdict yourself.
rg.verdictBad: Learning harness: the verdict of the demotion analyst was not applied: {error}. Nothing was changed. Call the agent again with the input from the context, or leave it: without a valid verdict nothing changes.
rg.transferLevel: Learning harness: [transfer-start {id}] is not possible, because {id} is at {level}. A transfer task is only possible at L2 or L3. Tell the learner and go on without a transfer task.
rg.transferBad: Learning harness: [transfer-ok {id}] does not count yet: the learner's last message does not pass the check ({reasons}). Ask the learner to explain the why in their own words. Do not give a lead yourself.
rg.transferHelp: [learning harness] The transfer task for {id} does not count: there was help (rung {rung}). A transfer task has to be done without help. Try a new one later.
rg.transferFailed: [learning harness] Transfer task for {id} not passed. Practise the gaps Claude named, and try a new transfer task later.
ss.unreadable.user: Learning harness: .learning/skills.json is unreadable. All project code is treated as L2 until it is fixed.
ss.unreadable.claude: LEARNING HARNESS: skills.json could not be read ({error}). Treat all code as L2 and ask the learner to fix the file.
ss.placementOpen: (placement open: L2 ladder until the first task)
ss.step.reviews: Mention today's reviews ({ids}) and offer to do one first: a short retrieval exercise without help (~5 min), on a different topic than before. Afterwards the learner records `review <id> pass|shaky|fail` themselves.
ss.step.pending: {n} tasks wait for an explanation in the learner's own words ({list}). Ask for that explanation; they only count afterwards.
ss.step.signal: Briefly point out what is going well{wins}{advice}.
ss.step.signal.advice: , and name the promotion proposals: {list}. Never change the record yourself
ss.step.goal: Ask: what is your goal today and which skill does it belong to? Ask for confidence (1-5) about one concrete exercise, for example: "How confident are you that you can finish <exercise> without help (1-5)?", not about the skill in general.
ss.ritual.resume: Session resumed or compacted: do not ask about the plan again, but stick to the levels below.
ss.active: LEARNING HARNESS ACTIVE (see CLAUDE.md for the full rules). Today: {day}.
ss.noExam: No exam date set (learner: `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs setting examDate YYYY-MM-DD`).
ss.levels: Default level for unmapped code: {level}. Reviews only at L4 (Fibonacci intervals): nothing at the session start; when such a skill comes by, the hook says so.
ss.table.head: | id | skill | level | solved (≤ rung 2, last 10) | paths / keywords |
ss.closeWithDiary: Close with /diary when the learner stops or says "done".
cli.badLevel: Level must be L0, L1, L2, L3 or L4.
cli.row.due: (review ready: do it yourself when it comes by)
cli.status.reviews: Reviews (L4) that are ready: {list}. You do not do them separately: the next time such a skill comes by in your work, you do it yourself, without AI.
cli.status.pending: Tasks waiting for an explanation in your own words: {list}
cli.status.lapsed: Skipped (explanation not given right away, does not count): {list}
cli.status.confirm: confirm: type "yes, promote {id}" in the chat
cli.status.declined: (you said no; comes back after new evidence)
cli.set.pending: Not changed: {n} task(s) of {id} still wait for your explanation in your own words ({tids}). Explain in the chat why your solution works; then it is possible.
cli.review.shaky: {id}: shaky, interval stays the same -> next review {date}
cli.review.fail: {id}: failed, interval 2 steps back -> next review {date}
cli.micro.nested: A microskill belongs to a main skill, not to another microskill.
cli.done: Task logged for {id} [{tid}], highest rung {rung}. It only counts once you explain in the chat, in your own words, why it works.
cli.lapsed: You start another exercise: the open explanation of {list} lapses (skipped, does not count).
cli.untask: {id}: last logged task voided{tid}. Now {ok}/{n} solved. (Shown in the diary.)
cli.correct.unknown: Unknown task '{tid}'. The task ids are in the output of check.mjs and in the diary.
cli.correct.usage: Usage: correct <task-id> rung <1-5> "reason"  or  correct <task-id> void "reason"
cli.correct.onlyUp: Task {tid} is already at rung {rung}. Corrections only go up: lowering it would make the evidence look better than it was.
cli.correct.rung: {id} [{tid}]: rung {from} -> {to}{failed}. Now {ok}/{n} solved. (Shown in the diary.)
cli.correct.void: {id} [{tid}] voided. Now {ok}/{n} solved. (Shown in the diary.)
cli.replay.usage: Usage: replay <transcript.jsonl> [--dry-run]. The transcript of a session is <session-id>.jsonl: in the subfolder projects of ~/.claude, or in your backup.
cli.replay.notOpen: [{tid}] not needed: this task does not exist or already counts.
cli.replay.failed: ✗ {id} [{tid}]: the explanation does not pass the hard check: {reasons}. Not logged.
cli.replay.wouldLog: ✓ {id} [{tid}]: both keys pass, would be logged.
cli.replay.logged: ✓ {id} [{tid}]: both keys pass, logged as explained (source: replay).
cli.replay.dryRun: --dry-run: {n} task(s) would be logged. Nothing was changed.
cli.replay.done: Done: {n} task(s) recovered. Every recovered event has source: replay.
cli.override.done: Override for {id} active until {until}. Shown in the diary.
cli.paths.usage: Usage: paths <id> add|remove "<glob>", e.g. paths ood.associaties add "ood-opdrachten-01/09-*/**"
cli.paths.micro: {id} is a microskill and has no paths: the guard uses the level of {parent}. Give the path to {parent}.
cli.paths.bad: Invalid path '{glob}'. Use a relative path inside the project, with / (e.g. exercises/09-*/**).
cli.paths.also: Note: {list} has the same path. With the same priority and length, the skill that comes first in skills.json wins. Remove it there with: paths <id> remove "{glob}"
cli.setting.usage: setting examDate YYYY-MM-DD | stuckTimerMinutes <number> | idleMinutes <number> | defaultLevel L0..L4 | course "<course>" | language nl|en | autoDemote true|false
cli.usage: Commands: list | status | set | review | add-micro | done | untask | correct | override | setting | paths | replay  (see the top of skill.mjs)
check.noTests: ✗ Build failed or no tests found: NO tests ran.
check.tipBuild: Tip: fix the compile error first; as long as it does not build, no test runs.
check.buildNoted: (Compile error noted as the starting point of this folder: a test that is green at the first build that works counts as new green.)
check.sdkMismatch: ⚠ {file} asks for SDK {sdk} (rollForward: {rollForward}), but the project targets {tf}. Your IDE may then use an SDK that cannot build this project, and show no errors. Ask your teacher whether you may set "rollForward": "latestMajor" in global.json.
check.restored: ↺ Green again: {tests}. These were green before, so this is a repair after a relapse and does not count as a new task.
check.baseline: (First run for this folder: this is the baseline, nothing is logged as a task yet.)
check.writtenFirst: (First run in this folder, and the code was written in this session: this green counts as new green. Tip: from now on, run check.mjs first, before you write code.)
check.noSkill: New green: {tests}. No skill found for {dir}: tag your prompt with #id or log it with `skill.mjs done <id>`.
check.logged: Logged as a task for {id} [{tid}], highest rung {rung}
check.logged.help: — with a lot of help, does not count as independent.
check.explain: Only counts after your explanation in your own words: why does it work now? (Claude judges, the hook checks.)
check.signal: After your explanation you can move up: {id} {from} → {to} ({text}). The harness then makes the proposal; confirm with "yes, promote".
check.transfer: After your explanation only the transfer task is missing ({text}): {show}
install.usage:
Usage:
  node harness/install.mjs <target-folder> [--map ood] [--lang nl|en] [--course "<course>"] [--exam YYYY-MM-DD] [--dry-run] [--yes]
  node harness/install.mjs <target-folder> --update [--dry-run] [--yes]

Without --yes the script only shows what would happen.
install.noTarget: the target folder does not exist: {dir}
install.selfTarget: do not install into the harness folder itself
install.badManifest: {file} is not valid JSON. Fix or remove the file.
install.already: the harness is already in this folder. Use --update to update the code.
install.notInstalled: there is no harness in this folder yet. Install it first without --update.
install.badLang: language must be nl or en
install.updateNoSettings: --exam and --course only apply when installing. Use `skill.mjs setting` afterwards.
install.noTranslation: {file}: no translation in '{lang}' yet, the Dutch version is used.
install.noSkill: a skill (diary or mastery-check) is missing from the harness
install.badSettings: .claude/settings.json is not valid JSON. Fix the file first; nothing was changed.
install.gitignoreComment: # Learning harness: do not share personal learning data and backups
install.note.obsolete: no longer in the harness, backup
install.note.mergeSettings: your own settings stay, hooks of the harness updated, backup
install.note.gitignoreBackup: exclude learning data and backups, backup
install.head: Learning harness {version} · {mode} in {dir}
install.legacy: · older install without a manifest found
install.upToDate: Everything is up to date. Nothing was changed.
install.needYes: Nothing was changed. Run it again with --yes to carry this out.
